text: Our meetup group Matters of Taste visited Cholita Taqueria on 5/19/19 for their unlimited Sunday brunch. Members enjoyed it so much that a return was planned for today Memorial Day since they closed on Sunday probably due to the race traffic. Unfortunately it was a disaster! We arrived promptly at 11 a.m. when the doors opened. Since there were 16 in our party in an effort to be less bother to the kitchen we decided to order as a group so everyone could taste multiple items on the menu. Immediately upon arrival our organizer put in our appetizer order for the table; 3 orders of Queso Fundido, some Mexican Street Corn and 3 Breakfast Tlayuda. I would assume that this was one of the first orders sent into the kitchen if not the first. The Breakfast Tlayuda's were large and 3 of them allowed everyone in our group to sample it. Not bad...nice and crunchy with lots of toppings. The Queso Fundido while a bit crispy on the outer edge was far from being hot and bubbly...in fact the cheese in the middle wasn't even melted!! We each passed around the ears of corn and cut some off the cob and boy was it delicious!! Prior to her unexpected departure Sigi had also placed an order for 16 Baja Fish Tacos and consulted with the group and asked our waiter to put in an order again for the table of '64 total items'...which our waiter then advised us that he didn't even give to the kitchen staff as 'an order for that many items would overwhelm them and no-one else would get any food'. This was a recurring theme from him and my thought was that if your restaurant seats x number of people and you offer an unlimited brunch you should be able to execute it even if every seat in the house is filled vs beating up on patrons who are there paying your wages. It was as though he expected an apology from us because we were there 'keeping others from getting their food'...not a great feeling. Considering that if each of the 16 of us would have placed an order individually for assorted tacos of our choice the kitchen would have had to prepare 32 tacos...not just 16 of one type so I found this to be very strange. Oh and I didn't mention that the ONLY food we were served in 1 1/2 hours were the shared appetizers and fish tacos mentioned above. At this point several of our party paid their checks and left. Our waiter then asked if we wanted to move down and consolidate, but he never bussed the table so we could do so. Finally, I pushed some glassed, plates, etc to the end of the table and wiped it down myself so we could squeeze together. We were then advised by our waiter he would take orders from each of us individually for one item off of the menu at a time. So we each placed an order for one item. Then we waited and waited and waited some more. No food came out from the kitchen. Then our waiter came back and told us to just go ahead and order 2 or 3 items each. At that point I wasn't sure what was happening to our orders...was the kitchen staff throwing them away...was he just not turning them in...perplexing. Personally, I placed an order for myself 4 times for the Mexican Style Crispy Chicken Milanese Sliders. i also requested the Sweet Corn Tamales and an order of Cinnamon Churros. At around 2 hours into our dining experience food began being delivered to our table. The Sweet Corn Tamales were outstanding but the Milanese Chicken Sliders weren't sliders at all. The sandwich was actually served on bread I normally associate with Cuban sandwiches. Since I had been warned about the spice level I was surprised that there was no heat to this sandwich at all which makes me wonder if it was prepared correctly. The chicken itself was crispy around the edges but soggy in the middle. Not something I would order again. At 2 1/2 hours after the manager became involved we did receive several Chocolate Mexican Waffles and orders of Churros, along with to-go boxes as we all were eager to get on with our other plans for the day. The Churros were pretty typical but the Chocolate Mexican Waffle was the bomb...light airy and with just the right chocolate flavor. Without the intervention of the manager --- thank you, thank you, thank you!! I'm not sure we would have received any food beyond our appetizers and fish tacos. It was also appreciated that he did mark our bills down to help make up for the poor service from the staff. Having hoped for a similar experience as the one our group had on 5/19/19 where they tried virtually every dish on the brunch menu I was a bit disappointed but enough of the food was tasty that I will probably give it another try...however, the beauty of going with a group is the ability to taste more dishes than you would be able to if dining alone or with only a small party. Oh, and by the time we paid our checks and got out the door we had been there for 3 hours. Hope they get the kinks worked out so patrons can have a more pleasant experience in the future.

text: The bubble tea we had from Tea Do was good. We enjoyed it. One of our friends, who currently lives in Philly, brought us here. It was a good choice. Another one of our friends, who used to live in Philly, considers this Philly's first "legit" bubble tea place. It opened in 2012. It's located in Chinatown, just one block north of Friendship Gate: https://www.yelp.com/biz/chinatown-friendship-gate-philadelphia. Outside, the corner storefront has a cool mural of a dragon. Inside, the place was packed. Almost every seat was taken - and this was on a Sunday night around 8:10pm. Like a lot of bubble tea shops, Tea Do isn't big, but it does have seating. There are a handful of high tables and low/coffee tables. Several years old now, there's nothing too remarkable about the interior. The menu is sizable with over 76 drinks to choose from. They include Tea Do specialties (special drinks unique to this brand), smoothies, milk bubble tea, popping bubble drinks, green tea drinks, black tea drinks, and aloe vera drinks. All drinks come in regular and large sizes. Most specialties and smoothies run $4.25 each for regular and $5.25 each for large, milk teas $3.50 regular / $4.50 large, and other drinks $3.75 regular / $4.75 large. There are 17 topping options and 16 of them cost $0.50 each (white pearl jelly is $0.75). In addition to the regular menu, there was a blackboard menu on the counter. During our visit, it advertised Tiger milk tea, winter melon green tea, Johnny tea, and chrysanthemum tea plus apple and yogurt popping boba and almond milk substitute. There was no description of the Tiger and Johnny teas, so you'd have to ask the staff. I tried three drinks: * Grasshopper (large, $5.25) * Taro bubble milk tea (large, $4.50) * Oolong bubble milk tea (regular, $3.75) I enjoyed all the drinks and would recommend all three of them. Across the board, I thought the tea and topping quality was good. Good tea flavor and fresh, appetizing toppings with ideal textures. The Grasshopper was different than what I'm used to (I usually order milk bubble teas). The Grasshopper is made with green tea, green apple, pear, green tea jelly, and lychee jelly. The drink was mildly sweet, a little bit tart, ice cold, and very refreshing. It hit the spot for me. I think my fiancee liked it the best of the drinks we ordered. The beans were a delicious healthy touch and plenty of them. My wife had the gnudi and added chicken. It was definitely different, she's a picky eater and loved it. I also stole a bite of hers and I think I may try that next. They also had a boulenaisse that I want to try. I changed my mind back and forth with the pork. They have a nice menu and plenty to chose from. We'll definitely be back. With 2 appetizers, 4 meals, and 2 glasses of wine, the bill came to $120 (without tip), so not cheap but not overly expensive. I would put it a step above Sip85 over by East Lake. Finally lamb ribs are inevitably fatty and this version was as well but it was undeniably tasty. Paired with a rice pilaf, it served well with the lamb to soak up all the fantastic juices from the lamb. The Dry Rub Chicken was equally impressive. text: Despite the rating, I actually really enjoy the food here. The food is good. The portion sizes are enough for everyone to try a piece of everything without feeling too full. I've been here four times total, with one of them being during soft opening with a group of friends. The food was significantly better during then. The second time was with my sister and the food was still pretty good then, too, but there was a server that kept bothering us about our food. Not really bothering, but she kept asking "how's everything? or "can I help you with everything" which normally would be fine, but if you ask every couple minutes (I'm not exaggerating), then it gets excessive. She literally asked us how everything was while I got started on eating a fish ball and then went to the next table and asked how everything is and then went back to us to ask the same question, and I was still chewing my fish ball. At that point, we started counting how many times she asked, and it was around 10-12 times within a two hour eating period. Please just let me finish my food. The third time I went was fine. I had no complaints except for the wait time which ended up being an hour & a half for four people. I guess that's okay, and it helps that Dave & Buster's is across the street. The fourth time was when I had real issues. It was my first time going during lunch hours, and everything was nice & prompt. I was with my friend who's a vegetarian, and we only opted for hot pot. There's plenty of vegetables and options for vegetarians. We had separate pots, so I could order any meat dish I want without disrupting her diet. We had ordered fried tofu which we both shared and decided that we wanted more. When the second batch arrived, I had noticed that it looked different from the first batch. The server also looked hesitant before placing it down on our table but ended up giving it to us anyway. The first batch looked like those fried soy puffs and the second one looked to me like actual tofu that's been fried which could also resemble fish tofu. I was eating a fish ball before taking a bite of the tofu, so I figured the fishiness was just from my fish ball. I was wrong. My friend who's been vegetarian for six years now took a bite and told me it tasted like fish and spit it back out. I pretty much insisted she was wrong, but I asked the server to come over and double checked with him to see if this was fried tofu and or fish tofu, and his words were "it should be fried tofu, but I can check for you if you want," and I opted not to check because I felt like it was probably just in her head. I was wrong. I took a bite of the tofu after drinking water and became unsure and then finally asked the waiter a second time to go check with the kitchen to see if it's really regular fried tofu. Also, at this point, my friend found a hair in her food (her hair was tied up, so I really don't think it was hers, and it's too short to be either of ours) Waiter came out with good news and bad news with the bad news being that to our dismay, the fried tofu we've been eating was actually fish tofu, and the good news being that we get 10% off our meal. I don't mean to sound entitled but 10% was $3.40. I'd be okay paying full price for my meal since I enjoyed it, but she's vegetarian, and she didn't eat much after finding out the fact that she ate fish. Telling her she gets 10% off her meal doesn't feel redeemable. The manager ended up coming out and apologizing for the hair but said nothing about the fish tofu incident. Overall, I would personally come back because like I said, I enjoy the food, but please watch out if you have any dietary restrictions.

First, I don't find it acceptable to bring me a glass of sparkling wine, that is flat as flat can be. It was clearly more than 4 days old, and did not have a single bubble (which should be super obvious when you pour it!!! - and you pour it in a wine glass and not a flute?? Your people in beverages should know this, and should manage their wine better! When I asked for a new glass from a new bottle, it took 11 minutes to replace it. Seriously - 11 minutes? After you make a mistake like that - have some ownership and get it done in at least 5 minutes (it wasn't that busy). Second, the wine list was a major fail - sorry - it just was. When someone in our group made a lot of requests on their food order, you don't roll your eyes. Look, I get it, I want to roll my eyes sitting with them, but I'm not the server, so show some professionalism. "Server" means serve the customer, not serve the kitchen. Otherwise, give me a counter to order from! The kitchen executed everything on the menu we ordered very well - no complaints (there were 6 of us, and we ordered maybe 10 dishes), but, the menu was nothing to get excited about. My thought was if we were in some run of the mill city, maybe it would be a really nice meal. But in NOLA, with the options you have - that menu does not remotely bring me back.

text: Man, I totally wished I had thought to look up this company's reviews before I bought anything from them. Like so many other people here, I got suckered into believing that this "family owned business" cared about the animals they were selling. They obviously don't. I only bought 2 Red Devil Crabs (Geosesarma sp.) for $31.76 ($15.88 each). I also paid for an ice pack for $1 (which was provided) and an insulated styrofoam box for $9 (which was also provided). The shipping cost for their proposed "fastest" method of shipping cost me $36. Both crabs arrived dead. There are a few reasons why this shipment was a disaster: 1. Shipping is done through USPS and they don't really have a true overnight service. The shipment took 2 days to get to me because of my location. If you read their shipping options, it becomes clear why it was worded the way it is. They technically didn't lie, but they are not really upfront with their shipping methods and do not mention that they actually use USPS as their shipping method. Their shipping options read like a test question on an exam that you have to read carefully or you will get tricked into picking the wrong answer. If you're reading too fast, you will believe that they use a true overnight courier service when they DO NOT. They shouldn't be shipping sensitive animals like fish and small invertebrates using 2 day courier services from USPS. They SHOULD ONLY be using OVERNIGHT services from companies like FedEx or UPS and should have options to have the packages held for pickup (again, which they do not). 2. The ice pack they sent in the package arrived warm and was practically worthless. 3. They do not communicate or coordinate with their customers as to when they should ship. If they had returned my email asking them when they were going to ship the crabs, I would've told them to hold the package for pickup because of the heat we're experiencing right now, or I would've added more ice packs. The other thing that irks me about this company is that it took them 2 weeks to send my order out, and there was no communication as to what the status of the order was. I placed an order on 6/28/2019 and got it today, 7/12/2019. Status updates on my order in my account was worthless. It still to this day says that the order is being assembled. I had also put a note in the order requesting 1 male and 1 female. They ended up shipping 2 females without letting me know about it. I felt that they ignored the notation I sent them, and just did whatever was convenient for them.

It was scheduled for 9:00 AM on January 13, and they sent an email confirming the appointment which noted that it would be 9:00 AM - 11:00 AM (120 mins). Just before that occurred, I pulled up the email to confirm that I had my date/time correct, and I noticed that they booked my detail out in Donelson! I called the Donelson location to explain my situation, and the manager said that if I drove to Donelson, they would get my car right in. text: What can I say about Fazoli's. It isn't just the unlimited breadsticks that make this place, it is the food itself. The food at Fazoli's is as good as any Italian fine food restaurant without the linen tablecloths and the high price. I had the Classic Sampler which includes the meat lasagna, spaghetti, and the fettuccini with Alfredo sauce. I love their meat lasagna! So many restaurants, including Olive Garden, ruined lasagna by using sausage for the meat instead of beef. I could definitely make a whole meal out of the fettuccini but its probably not a good idea calorie wise ;-) My wife likes the Fettuccine Alfredo too, my sister likes the Chicken Gnocchi Soup, my granddaughter went for the slice of pizza and loved it. We all enjoyed the bread sticks. The food was served quickly and piping hot. The service was excellent, she came around a couple times to see if we needed anymore breadsticks or anything else. You really cannot beat this place if you want fresh, hot, and cheap. Plus it is really good food. This place will be a regular stop for us. Hey, and don't forget you can order ahead and pick up or order there to take home. Great option after work when too tired or just don't want to cook. Wont break and bank and much better option than hamburgers and fries.

text: Awesome! We had a blast! A few quick tips: Book online. Park in the marina lot and put a quarter in the meter. Head over to H20 and they'll give you a 4 hour parking pass for $4. You'll have time to keep the vehicle parked and grab a bite after the tour. Leave your phone behind; they have secure storage. Tip your guide. We did the tour on a Thursday morning in October. It was my wife and I and another couple. I jokingly told my wife: "I got us a semi private tour!" What we liked about H20 was they had a covered space in the marina. This made filling out paperwork, gearing up, storing your stuff a lot easier. I'm sure you know this by now, but the FLA sun is HOT...even in October. The tour was a blast. We left the marina, went under the causeway bridge and blasted around a few islands. We had time for some free riding mid tour and our guide took pics of us on his phone (he sent them to us right after the tour). On the way back, we went by Clearwater beach. Our guide (William) was awesome! He and I stayed up front and went at a good clip. If the others got a bit behind, he'd do a few circles until they caught up and we were back on the throttles again. They have nice Yamaha machines here. They were all in good shape and well taken care of. Renters were on 1,000cc machines, the guide had the 1,800cc machine. (Wonder if they allow those to be rented? ; ) ) If you are a couple doing this, renting two machines is a good option. It allows everyone to go at their own pace. The couple that was with us stated they wished they went for two machines vs riding two up. All in all, this was a lot of fun! It's one of the things I tell people about back home when they ask: "How was your trip to Clearwater?:

I opted for the sparkling antioxidant tea ( super healthy) and it was delicious. I ordered the ancient grains bowl and added steak. Omg it was amaaaaazeballs! The steak was cooked exactly how I wanted it ( super juicy). The cilantro sauce ( I think that's what it was) just worked so well with all the ingredients and it tasted super yummy. All the ingredients tasted fresh.the food is super healthy but the taste is unbeatable. If you're not convinced about eating clean and healthy, this place will change your mind. Let me just add that I went back again and tried the roasted cauliflower ( charted cauliflower) and it didn't disappoint. It was delicious. I had the same bowl again ( hahahahaha). I ordered a dessert ( flourless chocolate cake) with a cappuccino ( fat free milk). I don't usually like flourless because I feel like the desserts always taste dense. But this cake was freakin delicious. Don't judge but I devoured it in like minutes. The cappuccino came hot ( which I specifically asked for). I hate cold coffee. ( only if it's intentionally that way - like a cold brew). All in all the service and the food was just superb. I felt good after eating my meal. This is my " go to spot" now. I just hope that it stays this way. The only recommendation that I have is that I would really looooove it if they had French fries ( ovebaked). Sometimes you just want some French Fries with a burger ( which I'm planning on ordering on my next visit). If you haven't tried this place out.... go!

text: Holy moly, Wilson's Secret Sauce lives up to the hype and the sauce itself is bomb af. First off, the husband-wife team who own this spot are SO nice and hospitable. It's warm and inviting, and a cute little pig collection arranged to the left of the kitchen, along with some of the other decorations, lends a hint of kitsch. The BBQ dished up here is top tier. We ordered a two meat platter to-go because we couldn't decide between brisket and pulled pork. Let me tell you, the flavors of the roast pork and smokey brisket were insane. Plus, both meats were just so tender and melt-in-your-mouth delicious. The roast pork was incredibly succulent and the brisket cut easy with a butter knife. Generous portions, too! One platter fed two people, and there was even a bit of pulled pork left over. And the Secret Sauce? It was sweet, spicy, tart, zesty, and highly addictive. We unabashedly scraped the two plastic cups clean and I may have licked my fingers... For sides, we picked mac 'n cheese and coleslaw. The stovetop style mac was deceptively cheesy -- I quickly realized that most of the cheese was hiding at the bottom. It was a tasty rendition worth repeating. Getting a bit of meat and mac together on the same fork and then dipping it into the sauce made for an intensely enjoyable bite. The coleslaw unfortunately had way too much mayonnaise for my liking. And I'm a lover of mayo! I also noticed that the cornbread was a little dry. But the cherry cheesecake pudding I picked for dessert? It had me feeling all warm and nostalgic inside. This pudding so reminded me of the Pennsylvania Dutch version of cherries jubilee (aka cherry delight), which I've adored since childhood. The cherries had the ideal tartness, which balanced out the sweetness of the cheesecake pudding. Total bliss. I'm glad I finally visited and I'll certainly be back, probably to dine in next time and chow down on a brisket cheesesteak. The meats I tried here are fantastic, and as the main attraction, they obviously matter most. But I also can't get that Secret Sauce out of my head, and the same goes for the cherry pudding dessert. I was sad to see Rigatoni's Crabcakes shut their doors awhile back, but I'm happy to have Wilson's take their place.

text: Gangnam Street Food is the newest Korean eatery to hit the K-mall area in the Southside Edmonton. If you haven't been there yet, it's a strip mall that has been overtaken by Korean businesses (mainly restaurants). You can find Let Eat Snow, Miga, Ginseng, and Korean/Japanese grocery store A-mart within steps of each other. Gangnam is owned by Mirae Investment Inc, a group that also owns Let Eat Snow, A-mart, Doobaeki, and Baekjeong Korean BBQ House. Gangnam introduces a new Korean eatery concept that hasn't be found here yet: Korean street food. Their menu focuses on smaller portions of food that can be enjoyed quickly for an inexpensive price of $4 to $10 each. I was told that in Korea, these types of eateries are found near schools to cater to students (that student budget life). Although the portions may appear small, I left feeling quite full! The food items in my post are from the tasting event that I attended last weekend. There will be more items on their actual menu such as kimbap (Korean sushi rolls), eomukguk (Korean fish cake soup), corn cheese, Korean spicy noodles with cheese, and more. At the tasting event, I was able to try six items from their menu. One of these items was dak-gang-jung (crispy Korean fried chicken) which I wasn't able to take an individual photo of. This was actually my favourite item of the night! The fried chicken pieces were boneless and juicy on the inside. The outside was very crispy and topped with a honey mustard sauce. There will be more flavours on the actual menu so stay tuned! Everyone at my table loved the Korean style hot dog! Similar-looking to a corn dog, the exterior is made of regular dough and breaded. As quoted, "the chef is very focused on the dough's texture to make it the best" and this was evident with every bite. There was a slight crisp from the breading, while the dough's texture had a nice chew. The inside had a hot dog, and if you'd like, you can also get it with mozzarella cheese for a cheesy texture! Personally, I don't like mozzarella cheese but I can see why everyone else at my table enjoyed it. I have yet to find a Korean restaurant that doesn't serve dduck bo kki (spicy Korean rice cakes). At Gangnam, the rice cakes and fish cakes are stir-fried in their special spicy sauce. The cakes had an enjoyable, chewy texture while the sauce wasn't too spicy. You can't go wrong with this Korean classic. I also recommend using the sauce as a dipping sauce for other items. I tried two of the four skewers that will be on their menu. The chicken skewer was dipped in their special Korean bulgogi sauce and the pork belly was brushed with their special super spicy sauce. Trust me, they didn't lie when they called it super spicy. I was only able to take a small bite of their pork belly skewer because I can't really handle spice! The cup bap is Gangnam's version of bibimbap. Served in a cup instead of a traditional hot stone bowl, it's meant to be enjoyed quickly or taken to-go. The one that I tried had spam and sausage in it, as well as stir-fried kimchi, bean sprouts, corn, lettuce, and a pan-fried egg. Mix it all together and you got yourself a meal. I actually really liked the mini sausages in the cup bap and I'm sure spam lovers will enjoy the spam. The portion might not seem like a lot because of the cup size but it will probably fill you up. They will have six kinds of cup bap on their menu so I'm excited to see what else they come up with! Our meal ended with a ho dduck, which is a Korean style pancake filled with melted cinammon and sugar filling. It was served hot, and reminded me of a cinammon bun. I really liked it! Gangnam officially opens to the public on January 24, 2019. I enjoyed their "fast-casual" concept and will probably stop by again if I'm in the area and craving a quick Korean bite!

text: So I'm a Delaware bitch. Iron Hill was a notable presence on UD campus' main street. We spent all day packing up our things prior to the move and left around 9pm to catch them before the kitchen closes. At that hour, most of the tables were empty and we were able to enjoy a lot of attention from the server. We were seated by the window with good seats to observe the homeless man nodding into the street's garbage can. There's a lot of good stuff on the menu, just the appetizers alone offer buffalo cauliflower, margherita flatbread, hummus, pretzel sticks, lettuce wraps, guac and much more for my meat-eating friends. We settled on the nachos, brussels sprouts, and my carnivorous GF ordered the philly cheesesteak rolls (bc how could you not?). The nachos just on presentation alone were scrumptious. The chips were crisp and covered with not just melted cheddar but also that delicious white mexican cheese that resembles crumbled feta (whatever that shit is). There were ACTUAL BEANS and ACTUAL JALAPENOS instead of that pickled shit. There was also a spritz of a delicious, creamy, white sauce. Who doesn't like white, creamy sauce? To top it all off, there were two massive dollops, one of sour cream (creme fraiche if you want to be a fancy bitch) and one of GUAC. Did I mention the diced tomatoes? (that no one really cares about tbh). These were surprisingly good nachos from Iron Hill. The brussels sprouts were tasty but nothing special. I did appreciate the pecorino romano dusting on top. The philly cheesesteak rolls, and don't take my word for it because I am an onion-despising vegetarian were meh. My flesh-eating companion, however, enjoyed them tremendously (confirmed verbatim that this comment is not an embellishment). I also got a cocktail which I do not recall but it was something with tequila and beer and it was delicious. Their tap menu is also impressive. OMG I almost forgot that we also ordered the cauliflower tacos which on this particular evening were $1 (taco tuesday). I actually no longer see it on the menu however I do see "thai vegetable lettuce wraps" which appears to be similar, our tacos had an asian flare. This is a good place to stop by for a drank (if you're picky or like unusual beers) and a meal!

I do wish we had chosen Hot or Damn Hot!! for one of our meals, as we found the Medium to be a nice heat but nothing spicy. We went with the SM White Plate and the classic Hot Chicken Sandwich, and chose the fries, potato salad, and mac n cheese for our sides. The chicken was perfectly cooked, juicy on the inside and a delicious crispy crust on the outside. It was easily some of the best fried chicken I've ever had. The fries were crisp and delicious, although a little heavily seasoned, the potato salad was good, and the mac and cheese was delicious, taken up a notch by the inclusion of pimentos. We loved Hattie B's, and would definitely come back on another trip to Nashville. I would highly recommend a visit to anyone, regardless of if you like spicy food or not - there's a heat level for everyone here. The prices were fair for the portion sizes and the atmosphere was good. As I'm writing this now, I wish I was able to have some sent up to Wisconsin for lunch!

text: Service was fine, food was meh. The issue was not so much with the food or service, but with the whole structure of this place. It's a mess. This is not cafeteria dining. This place is an example of great idea, poor execution. 1) There is a server stand with 2 people that do nothing but point to the direction of your table. They don't walk you to your table, they don't get a high chair if you need it. They literally stand there, call you when a table is open, then point you to the ground floor or second floor. Why does that take 2 people? 2) Cafeteria style dining is when you can get different foods easily and then pay at the end. Not here. You have to go to each different vendor and order, pay, then get your food. Also, you tip before receiving your food so....how much should you tip? Who cares? This place doesn't care or they would have designed a better system. Poor execution. 3) When you do get a table inside, your server only brings you drinks. You still need to go get your food from the non-cafeteria style mess of restaurants. So, the server is only getting tips on drinks and you have to pay again after already paying for your food. The server is getting drinks that I could just go get myself while waiting for my food? Why would you design it this way? I'm pretty sure 80% of our time here was waiting on food, drinks, and the check. Poor execution. Colombus OH, Chicago IL, Seattle WA, NYC NY, these are all places that are doing this well. Here's what needs to happen. 1) Don't make people stand in line at each place. Get a software system that each vendor must use and patrons can place their order at one time for every vendor. Or, order your food at each place and then pay at the end (a worse option but still better than how it is now). A patron should be able to order Nachos and a hot dog at once. Otherwise, it's not cafeteria style, it's a food court. This would cause less confusion for the vendors, and it would make everything go so much faster since you aren't processing a payment 5 different times. Also, it would likely increase sales as I would have ordered more food from different vendors but was not willing to stand in line again. Currently, it actually punishes patrons for wanting to experience all of the diverse food options. 2) If you are going to have servers, then have them serve food and drink. Otherwise, get rid of servers. I'm already waiting on the food. It's not like it's saving any time to have them just bring drinks. It's okay to not have servers. That's how most other cities do it. 3) I would assume most people are coming to Sun King to get some alcohol. Why not put it close to the door? This isn't a big deal, but it just shows that whoever designed this did not think through it. 4) Save your vendors time and have a central place for to-go containers, napkins, utensils, and condiments. This is just basic. There is currently no leverage of having 5 vendors in one spot. Even food courts do this. 5) Make it simple and enjoyable for patrons. We waited for 30 minutes to get a table to then be told we still need to wait in line and order our food. What?! What is the benefit of sitting inside? Please, please, go visit other, true cafeteria-style dining places and make changes. This could be so cool, but it's currently run like a madhouse.

text: Rainforest Cafe is a unique dining experience that is worth going out of your way for. The feel of being in the rain forest itself is just too much fun to miss. I love the animal displays, the lightning storms, the noises, and most of all how numerous waiters will repeatedly scream "VOLCAAAAANNOOOO" whenever someone orders that dessert. Said volcano dessert is basically icecream with chocolate cake/brownie. It's pretty good, but not the best I've ever had. The ribs here don't have much meat on them or much flavor to me and the Rotisserie Chicken was bland as well. The Parmesan was packed with flavor but it wasn't my thing. The Coconut Shrimp was great and I would like to order more of them next time. He came back with the same bowl, but it had just been washed off. The fruit was now dripping in water. The bowl had water in the bottom of it. I told him that it's not ok to rinse bad fruit and bring it back. He got defensive and insisted that's not what happened. Unfortunately, I have eyes and taste buds. This was not fresh fruit. The manager heard the commotion and offered to comp my meal but I had already paid. She was actually really nice about it. I'd come back if my book club was meeting here or stopping in for a coffee and chat with friends. But I don't think I'll be back to eat.

text: Ugh. I really wanted to like this place. I've walked by it countless times and thought about going in on numerous occasions. It's no secret that the ambiance is on point... but the good pretty much stops there. Came in for lunch with a reservation for restaurant week. We were seated pretty quickly and approached by our server in a reasonable amount of time. We ordered two house punches and a bellini. While they didn't have peach puree or liqueur, they were able to make a strawberry bellini. The drinks were tasty, but the alcohol was severely lacking, especially for $14 drinks. The punch was highlighted as a tequila drink, but I swear there wasn't an ounce in there. The first course took a while to come out, but it was definitely the highlight of the meal. Two of us decided on mushroom soup and one decided on a salad. The soup was my favorite part of the meal and I wish there was more of it. One of the whole mushrooms was vinegary and cut the creamy soup well. The salad was tasty and the mixed greens and seeds were yummy. The second course took even longer to come out, which was really frustrating, especially as we saw other tables getting their food much quicker. While we were waiting, we requested a bottle of wine, but were told they were served in carafes... unclear whether the carafe equaled a full bottle of wine, but if not, it would definitely be more cost effective to order by the glass. For food, we ordered two sea bass and one burger. The fish smelled fishy but tasted fine. The crispy skin was good, but the portion was small. The burger came out good, but it was served with a side salad... others who were also doing restaurant week had chips or fries, but our waitress never asked what my friend wanted... she had the salad to start, so she was hoping for anything BUT salad again. Another disappointment. The burger itself was good but also pretty small. Finally, dessert, which somehow took even longer. By that time we had been at lunch for nearly two hours! Two of us went with the ricotta pound cake with lemon-thyme (?) ice cream and poached pears, and one went with the blood orange sorbet with chocolate rice cakes. Both were disappointing. Pound cake is usually pretty heavy, but this was on another level. The ice cream accompaniment was good (it's hard to mess up ice cream), but it barely had flavor for being called lemon/thyme. The pears were good. My friend enjoyed her sorbet, but could barely bite into the rice cakes. Overall another underwhelming course. I was really excited to try this place but was unfortunately let down. Ambiance was good, but that was really the extent of it. I usually use restaurant week to try out places I haven't been to in the hopes of finding new spots to bring into my regular rotation, but we won't be back.
label: NEG
